chains <- 4; iter <- 4000 fit_dir <- "./data/processed/cv_fits" dir.create(fit_dir, showWarnings = FALSE) # posterior predictive checks (density overlay and mean), by group if given custom_ppc <- function(fit, group = NULL, ndraws = 100) { pal <- scale_fill_viridis_d(begin = 0.3, end = 0.8, alpha = 0.5, option = "mako") if (!is.null(group) && group %in% names(fit$data)) { p <- list(pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "dens_overlay_grouped", group = group), pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "stat_grouped", stat = "mean", group = group)) } else { p <- list(pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "dens_overlay"), pp_check(fit, ndraws = ndraws, type = "stat", stat = "mean")) } plot_grid(plotlist = lapply(p, function(x) x + pal + theme_classic()), ncol = 2) } ci <- function(x, digits = 2) paste0(round(median(x), digits), " [95% UI: ", round(quantile(x, 0.025), digits), "–", round(quantile(x, 0.975), digits), "]") ``` ::: # Purpose {.unnumbered} - Test whether the vocalizations of the focal bellbird are classified more often as the sympatric species it could have imitated than as their allopatric relatives, and more often than the vocalizations of other bellbirds - Test whether the classifications of the focal bellbird changed over time Classifications come from the cross-validated BirdNET classifiers of the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report. The fits are saved in `data/processed/cv_fits/`. # Cross-validated classifiers ## Design - All training and test clips were pooled and split into 5 folds grouped by recording (all clips of a recording in the same fold) and stratified by species, seed 123 - For each fold, the classifiers were trained on the other 4 folds (early stopping on a random 20% of the training clips) and classified the held-out fold, so every clip has a prediction from a model that never heard its recording - Training and classification used a 400–12,000 Hz bandpass - Hyperparameters were chosen by random search among 30 configurations drawn from the search space of BirdNET-Analyzer's built-in tuner; for each classifier, the simplest configuration within one standard error of the highest out-of-fold macro-averaged AUPRC was selected (rule set before seeing the results, without using the focal bellbird). See the [model fitting](birdnet_model_fitting.qmd) report - Per-species thresholds maximize F1 on the out-of-fold predictions. A clip is assigned to its highest-confidence species if it reaches that species' threshold, otherwise it is unassigned - The focal bellbird clips are classified by the 5 fold models of the selected configuration: confidences are averaged across models (ensemble) and the out-of-fold thresholds are applied ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} folds <- read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "folds.csv")) best_cfg <- with(read.csv(file.path(cv_dir, "selected_configurations.csv")), setNames(config, model))[models] data.frame(Classifier = model_labels[models], `Selected configuration` = best_cfg, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display}

Consistency is the variability within a time window (the recording day): for each clip, the mean cosine similarity of its embedding to each of the other clips of the same type recorded on the same day (day × type combinations with at least 5 clips). Higher values mean more consistent. Unlike the similarity to a centroid of the day's clips, the expected value of this mean pairwise similarity does not depend on the number of clips of the day (only its precision does), which matters because the number of own-song clips per day increased through the season. The model has the same structure as that of acoustic similarity. Three checks: the (log) number of clips of the day × type as a covariate; the residual SD modelled as a function of the (log) number of clips (the mean pairwise similarity of a clip in a large group is less noisy, so these clips get more weight, with the amount estimated from the data rather than fixed through weights); and a rarefied version in which each day × type combination is repeatedly subsampled to 5 clips (100 draws) and its mean pairwise similarity averaged across draws, modelled at the level of the combination. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} qc <- q_m qc$day_type <- paste(qc$day, qc$species) grp_n <- table(qc$day_type) qc <- qc[qc$day_type %in% names(grp_n)[grp_n >= 5], ] qc$n_group <- as.numeric(grp_n[qc$day_type]) # If the focal bellbird produced more than one dialect, and in proportions that changed through time, a day centroid that mixes dialects would make its own song look less consistent, and a shift towards the dialect closer to the reference recordings could look like an improvement. A BirdNET classifier was trained to discriminate the dialects of the reference bellbirds (annotated as Monteverde, Nicaragua, Panama and Talamanca; babbling left out), with the same pipeline as the species classifiers: 5-fold cross-validation grouped by recording and stratified by dialect (seed 123), bandpass 400–12,000 Hz, per-dialect thresholds maximizing F1 on the out-of-fold predictions, and the configuration chosen with the one-standard-error rule among the same 30 random configurations compared for the species classifiers (`MODELS=dialect bash scripts/birdnet_cv.sh`). This section quantifies how large a change the data can rule out, and whether a straight line through time hides a change that is not linear (e.g. an early improvement that then levels off). ## How large a change the data can rule out All measures and dates are standardized, so slopes are in SD of the measure per SD of date. A region of practical equivalence (ROPE) of ± 0.1 SD per SD of date was used, the conventional "negligible" standardized effect (Kruschke 2018). Given the length of the sampling season, this ROPE is equivalent to a change of about ± 0.1 × (season range in SD of date) over the whole season (see the table). Each slope is classified as: - **Change**: the 95% interval excludes zero - **Practically no change**: the 95% interval lies entirely within the ROPE - **Inconclusive**: neither (the data cannot tell a negligible change from a relevant one) The approximate minimum detectable slope is the slope that would be detected (95% interval excluding zero) with 80% probability given the posterior uncertainty: (1.96 + 0.84) × posterior SD of the slope. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rope <- 0.1 type_draws <- function(fit) { post <- as_draws_df(fit) base <- post$b_scalejulian_day
